newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg mum on Bulgaria Brady reports.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg mum on Bulgaria Brady reports.

text.p: SBC Warburg Swiss Bank Corp on Thursday declined comment on market reports that it had stopped making markets in Bulgarian Brady bonds.
Banking sources said the bank was now in the process of telling clients it was pulling out of that market after Bulgarian Brady bonds had plunged about 12 percent in just over a week.
"We have no official comment," an SBC Warburg spokesman said.
The reports had no impact on the markets.

Long an attraction for its high yield, Bulgarian Bradys have been by far the worst performer in a generally bouyant emerging debt market on fears that political and economic mismanagement in the country is making the threat of debt default very real.
The market went into panic on Wednesday after new President Petar Stoyanov told an audience in Brussels that his country may not be able to honour its debts without international help.
His comments sent the price of the bonds down by more than two cents, though they had stabilised by Thursday.

Protestors have been marching through Belgrade and other parts of the country for weeks, demanding the ruling Socialists hold early elections so that a government can get on with hauling the economy out of its hole and stave off the threat of hyper-inflation.
